verdict.rationale: Highnote documents API-driven card issuance per agent or workflow, programmable spend rules and velocity controls, and a unified ledger for balances and transactions, so an agent can operate the core of a card program through the GraphQL API or the beta Node SDK. The evidence shows no MCP surface and no scoped API credentials: the docs describe 'one key', and role-based permissions apply only to Dashboard users. Missing for 10: MCP server, scoped or least-privilege API credentials for agents, explicit card-update and balance or transaction read endpoints, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an agent can operate my card program — read balances and transactions, create and update cards, and adjust spend controls through the API or an MCP surface with scoped credentials

citations.quote: Issue cards per agent, workflow, or vendor via API. Each card closes automatically when the workflow ends. No manual provisioning.
Set velocity limits, merchant category restrictions, and per-transaction caps at the card, account, or program level.
Track money movement and balances with the integrated ledger.
The full payment lifecycle is available via API.
Spend rules let you automate logic on authorizations that permit or restrict transactions.
